headline: Bitcoin ended Wednesday's US session just above $60,000 after stocks clawed back a steep morning sell-off, while big research desks warn the crypto slide may not be over going into the Thanksgiving holiday.

market.asOf: Prices from Motley Fool's crypto wrap, published 5:06pm ET Wed 25 Nov (22:06 UTC), as of early evening US time. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 9 on CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index, checked when this edition was written.

stories.title: Wall Street claws back a 4% Nasdaq plunge; bitcoin ends the US day just above $60,000
stories.summary: AI and chip stocks crashed at Wednesday's open, on a day the US also proposed new tariffs, then buyers stepped in before Thanksgiving and the day ended mixed. Bitcoin, which has been moving with tech stocks, followed the same round trip.
points: Final closes on Wed 25 Nov: Dow 50,182.95 (+0.33%), S&P 500 7,182.78 (-0.25%), Nasdaq 23,585.80 (-0.62%), per Avalon Capital's closing snapshot.
At the morning low the Nasdaq was down more than 4%, about 20% below its record, per CoinDesk; Nvidia closed down 3.91%, per StockTitan.

CoinDesk reported bitcoin at $57,500 after the open and back above $60,000 by 2:24pm ET. At 5:06pm ET it was $60,139, up 0.66% on the day, with the rebound driven by forced closing of leveraged short bets, per Motley Fool.
The proposed tariffs on 14 economies are not in effect yet; hearings begin 25 January, per Decrypt.
US stock markets are closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday; crypto keeps trading around the clock on thin holiday volume.

stories.title: Galaxy withdraws its 'bear market is over' call as crypto's total value falls to its lowest since September 2024
stories.summary: Galaxy's research head took back his October call that the crypto bear market ended in June, and other veterans say this downturn feels different. Bitcoin funds are heading for their worst month on record.
points: Galaxy's Alex Thorn: "We withdraw the October call that the bear market ended in June." He is watching whether bitcoin's June closing lows hold ($58,525 daily, $59,517 weekly), per CoinDesk.
The whole crypto market was worth $2.08 trillion, its lowest since September 2024, and about $515 million of trading positions were liquidated in 24 hours, per The Block.
US spot bitcoin funds had $4.94 billion of net outflows in November through Tuesday, on track for their worst month since launch, per Decrypt.
Bitcoin was on track for its eighth weekly loss in a row, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: Washington: Democratic senators push the SEC to scrap its crypto rules, while the CFTC widens use of bitcoin and ether
stories.summary: Four Democratic senators asked SEC Chair Paul Atkins to withdraw two pro-crypto measures. On the same day, CFTC staff said some trading firms may count bitcoin, ether and stablecoins toward their capital needs.
points: Sens. Warren, Van Hollen, Tina Smith and Jack Reed want the SEC to withdraw its proposed "Regulation Crypto Assets" and its September "innovation exemption" for tokenized-securities venues, per The Block.
The proposal includes a startup exemption for offerings up to $5 million and a fundraising exemption up to $75 million, per The Block.
The senators say the exemption would create "a shadow stock market."
A CFTC staff advisory lets bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins, after a haircut, count toward a one-year operating-expense requirement for some exchanges and clearing houses, per The Block.

briefs.title: Tether's reserve cushion shrinks
briefs.summary: Losses on Tether's gold and bitcoin cut its reserve cushion from $7.95 billion on 30 Sep to about $2.26 billion on paper; USDT supply is $174.4 billion, down from a $190.4 billion peak, per Yahoo Finance.

briefs.title: A big holder dumps HYPE
briefs.summary: HYPE fell below $60, down nearly 8% in 24 hours, as Lookonchain tracked Abraxas Management selling 219,081 HYPE ($13.25 million), per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Franklin Templeton's crypto index fund adds HYPE
briefs.summary: The Franklin Crypto Index ETF (EZPZ) will add Hyperliquid's HYPE from 1 December, per an SEC filing reported by The Block.

briefs.title: Kraken's Krak opens a waitlist for US credit cards
briefs.summary: Two Visa Signature cards due in early 2027 offer up to 4% cashback in dollars or bitcoin, per The Block.

briefs.title: Ripple signs a Turkish bank for crypto custody
briefs.summary: Yapı Kredi became a Ripple custody client; Turkish rules require 95% of customer crypto to be held with a licensed custodian, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Miner CleanSpark sold more bitcoin than it mined
briefs.summary: CleanSpark sold 2,102 BTC against 1,708 mined in the quarter, holds 13,530 BTC and posted a $987 million fiscal-year net loss, per Cointelegraph.

briefs.title: Kalshi halts operations in Utah
briefs.summary: The prediction market stopped operating in Utah, per The Block.

briefs.title: Justice Department announces its largest-ever crackdown on crypto scam centers
briefs.summary: The DOJ says it targeted more than 800 defendants and froze more than $1 billion in stolen crypto, per The Block.
